## Introduction

This post demonstrates every feature available in this Distill-style blog. It covers typography, margin notes, citations, math, interactive charts, and code.

::: {.aside}
**Margin Note:** This is a margin note — it floats to the right on desktop and collapses inline on mobile, just like distill.pub.
:::

As shown in the original Distill journal, the key to great ML communication is combining beautiful typography with interactive explanations. See [@vaswani2017attention] for a canonical example of transformer architecture.

---

## Typography

The body uses **Georgia** serif for maximum readability. Headers use system sans-serif. Code uses **JetBrains Mono**.

You can write *italic text*, **bold text**, and `inline code` naturally.

> "The most important thing is that readers can understand the ideas." — Distill.pub

---

## Math & Equations

Inline math: $f(x) = \sigma(Wx + b)$

Block equations:

$$
\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
$$

The transformer attention mechanism [@vaswani2017attention] computes:

$$
\mathcal{L} = -\sum_{i} y_i \log(\hat{y}_i)
$$

---

## Code Blocks

Python:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class SelfAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embed_dim, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.attn(x, x, x)[0]
```

R:

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Interactive Charts (Observable JS)

```{ojs}
//| label: fig-interactive
//| fig-cap: "An interactive scatter plot. Drag the slider to filter."

viewof threshold = Inputs.range([0, 100], {
  value: 50,
  step: 1,
  label: "Filter threshold"
})

data = Array.from({length: 50}, (_, i) => ({
  x: Math.random() * 100,
  y: Math.random() * 100
}))

filtered = data.filter(d => d.x > threshold)

Plot.plot({
  marks: [
    Plot.dot(filtered, {x: "x", y: "y", fill: "steelblue", opacity: 0.7})
  ],
  x: {label: "X →"},
  y: {label: "↑ Y"},
  style: {fontSize: 12}
})
```

---

## Plotly Interactive Chart

```{python}
#| label: fig-plotly
#| fig-cap: "Interactive Plotly chart embedded in the article."

import plotly.graph_objects as go
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 4*np.pi, 200)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=x, y=np.sin(x), name="sin(x)", mode="lines"))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=x, y=np.cos(x), name="cos(x)", mode="lines"))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white",
    height=350,
    margin=dict(l=40, r=20, t=20, b=40),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02),
    xaxis_title="x",
    yaxis_title="f(x)"
)
fig.show()
```

## Margin Figure

**Figure 1:** A margin figure, anchored to the right of the body text on desktop screens.

Margin figures are a signature feature of Distill. They allow you to place supplementary visual context alongside the relevant text without interrupting the reading flow.

## Conclusion

This post demonstrates the full range of features available in this Distill-style blog:

- Margin notes and margin figures
- Hover citations and footnotes
- Math equations (KaTeX)
- Interactive charts (Observable JS + Plotly)
- Wide and full-page figures
- Code blocks with syntax highlighting
